development_data: Meta-signature from published gene lists: 42 breast cancer signatures (2002-2009) taken from GeneSigDB; the 117 genes present in more than four of the 42 lists (Venet list 111 symbols). The paper itself used no patient expression or outcome data to select genes; several constituent lists were themselves outcome-trained (e.g., van 't Veer 2002 NKI prognosis genes, Pawitan 2005 Stockholm, Loi 2008 tamoxifen cohorts, Wang 2005 Rotterdam, Paik 2004 NSABP).
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (van de Vijver 2002; OS and RFS, Kaplan-Meier and multivariate Cox).
evidence: Methods, 'Identification of common gene expression features among breast cancer signatures' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2978930/): "We selected the most relevant gene signatures derived from 42 breast cancer gene expression profiling studies (from 2002 to 2009) (see additional file 1)."; Results (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2978930/): "Of the 946 transcripts, 117 genes were identified in more than four studies, representing a set of the most frequents breast cancer biomarkers in this analysis (Fig. 1B)."; Methods, 'Gene expression meta-signature and survival analysis' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2978930/): "We selected van de Vijver data set due to the biological diversity of breast tumors included in this study.17 Briefly, van de Vijver's data set included 295 early-stage breast cancer samples (226 ER-positive and 69 ER-negative)"; same section (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2978930/): "In an unsupervised analysis, 295 tumor samples were grouped by similarity of the 117 gene list meta-signature by complete linkage clustering by using the Multi Experiment Viewer software. development_data: ES exp1 gene set (380 genes) taken from Assou et al. 2007 meta-analysis of human ES cell profiling studies (genes overexpressed in hES cells in 5 or more of 20 studies); no tumor data or outcome used to define it.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Six-study breast compendium of 1,211 tumors (van de Vijver NKI 295, Sotiriou 2006, Miller 2005 Uppsala, Chin 2006, Wang 2005, Desmedt 2007) for enrichment by grade/ER/size/subtype and by LN metastasis, distant metastasis and death; overall-survival Kaplan-Meier and random-effects meta-analysis in five studies: Miller (n=236), Chin (n=117), van de Vijver (n=295), Desmedt (n=147), Pawitan (n=159). Also glioblastoma and bladder data (grade only).

development_data: In vitro co-cultures of seven breast cancer cell lines and HMECs with fibroblasts; 42-gene interferon-response cluster induced when ER-negative cell lines were co-cultured with fibroblasts. No patient outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (29 matched spots; distant metastasis-free and overall survival; correlation with 70-gene, wound and hypoxia scores); Stanford/Norway advanced breast cancers (Sorlie 2001/2003; trend p=0.067); Vancouver tissue microarray, STAT1 immunohistochemistry in 353 patients (disease-specific survival).
evidence: Materials and methods, Human breast cancer dataset: 'The interferon response gene list consists of 42 genes represented by 49 image clones on the cDNA Stanford array.' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC2375029); Results, Genomic analysis of epithelial-mesenchymal interaction effects in human cancers: 'We therefore looked for this response in the expression patterns in published data from 295 early stage (stage I and II) breast cancer samples from the Netherlands Cancer Institute (NKI) [35] (Figures 6a,b and 7).' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC2375029); Results: 'We found that tumors with high expression levels of interferon-response genes had a significantly shorter metastasis-free survival (p = 0.0014; 58% at 10 years) and overall survival (p = 0.001; 59% at 10 years) than tumors with low expression levels' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC2375029)

development_data: CIN70: top 70 genes by integrated rank of correlation with total functional aneuploidy (tFA, an expression-derived aneuploidy score, no outcome) in three datasets: van 't Veer breast (NKI patients), Bild ovarian and Bild SCLC.
validation_data_named_in_paper: 18 datasets / 6 cancer types; breast: van 't Veer 2002, van de Vijver 2002 (NKI 295), Sotiriou 2006 JNCI (GSE2990), Wang 2005 (GSE2034), Bild 2006 breast; dichotomized at the dataset mean of summed signature expression. Signature significant in 12 of 18 datasets, including all five breast sets.
evidence: Abstract: 'We identified a signature of chromosomal instability from specific genes whose expression was consistently correlated with total functional aneuploidy in several cancer types. development_data: In vitro: 50 cultured fibroblast samples from 10 anatomic sites in 10% vs 0.1% serum (multiclass SAM, coordinate induction/repression), minus 165 genes periodically expressed in the HeLa cell cycle (Whitfield 2002). No patient data or outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Stanford/Norway locally advanced breast cancers (Sorlie 2001; 51 equivalently treated patients, metastasis and death); van 't Veer 2002 78 node-negative NKI patients (5-year distant metastasis, multivariable Cox); lung adenocarcinoma (Bhattacharjee 2001, n=62; Garber 2001); stage III gastric carcinoma (Leung 2002, n=42).
evidence: Results, Identification of a Stereotyped Genomic Response of Fibroblasts to Serum: 'these 512 serum-responsive and cell cycle-independent genes are operationally defined as the fibroblast core serum response (CSR).' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC314300); Results, Link between the Gene Expression Signature of Fibroblast Serum Response and Cancer Progression: 'Using published DNA microarray data from a study of gene expression patterns in a group of 78 early (tumor smaller than 5 cm, stage I and IIA) breast cancer patients (van 't Veer et al. 2002), we could segregate the patients into two groups based on expression of the fibroblast CSR genes in the biopsy samples. Tumors with the serum-induced signature had a significantly increased risk of metastasis over 5 y (p = 0.00046) (Figure 4A).' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC314300); Materials and Methods, Data analysis: 'In each set of patient samples, the samples were segregated into two classes based on the first bifurcation in the hierarchical clustering dendrogram.' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC314300)

development_data: In vitro: hypoxia (2% O2) and anoxia time courses in cultured human mammary epithelial cells, renal proximal tubule epithelial cells, endothelial and smooth muscle cells; a cluster of 253 clones (168 UniGene clusters) consistently induced by hypoxia in epithelial cells. No patient outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Renal tumors (n=41, histology only); Stanford/Norway locally advanced breast cancers (Sorlie 2001; 78 cancers, overall and relapse-free survival); NKI 295 (overall survival, distant metastasis-free survival, multivariable Cox with the 70-gene and wound signatures); 72 ovarian cancers.
evidence: Results, The Hypoxia Phenotypes in Human Cancers: 'Since carcinomas derive from epithelial cells, we selected a cluster of 253 individual elements (representing 168 unique Unigene clusters according to build number 172, released on 17 July 2004) that was consistently induced by hypoxia in cultured epithelial cells and will be referred to as the "epithelial hypoxia signature"' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC1334226); Results, The Hypoxia Phenotypes in Human Cancers: 'To assess the consistency and prognostic significance of the hypoxia response signature in an independent set of breast cancer samples, we analyzed a published data set from the NKI, which consisted of 295 early-stage breast cancer samples (stage I and II) [47].' and 'Tumors in the high hypoxia response group were associated with much poorer overall survival (p = 1.4 × 10−9) and higher risk of disease recurrence (p = 1.3 × 10−5) (Figure 4C)' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC1334226); Results, Prognostic Information Content of the Hypoxia Signature: 'To investigate whether an alternative threshold might improve predictive power, we refit our multivariate Cox model by including the hypoxia response score in a quantitative form, using natural cubic splines with four degrees of freedom.' and 'The results showed a strong positive trend over the range of hypoxia response scores in which most of the data occur, and indicate that a threshold value of zero was a reasonable choice.' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC1334226); Methods, Analysis of an Epithelial Hypoxia Signature in Human Cancers: 'Cross-checking gene names revealed 22 probes that could not confidently be contributed to genes in the original hypoxia signature. These were removed, resulting in 158 matched probes.' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC1334226)

development_data: Brd4 activation signature from mouse Mvt-1 mammary tumor cells ectopically expressing Brd4 vs beta-galactosidase (4 vs 3 clonal isolates, Mouse 430 2.0 arrays); 638 probe sets with P < 1e-7 mapped to 971 human U133 probe sets / 379 genes (Dataset S5). No patient outcome used.

development_data: NKI: 311 tumors (295 from van de Vijver 2002 plus 16 nonredundant tumors from van 't Veer 2002); within the ER/age-high subgroup (83 patients, all from the 295 cohort) 50 reporter genes were selected by correlation with metastasis outcome using iterative training-sample selection and leave-one-out cross-validation. Venet's 35 symbols correspond to these 50 reporters.
validation_data_named_in_paper: No independent cohort; leave-one-out and repeated random 3-fold splits within the same NKI ER/age-high patients; Kaplan-Meier analysis of metastasis-free and overall survival restricted to patients of the original 295 cohort.
evidence: Materials and Methods: 'Three hundred and eleven breast carcinoma samples that satisfied the selection criteria defined in ref. Specially, these samples include 295 samples from our cohort study ( 15 ) and 16 nonredundant samples from our initial study ( 3 ).' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/65/10/4059/517951); Materials and Methods, Feature selection and performance evaluation: 'Prognostic features were selected based on the training samples by their correlation to outcome and were reselected during each step of leave-one-out cross-validation.' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/65/10/4059/517951); Results: 'Within the ER/age high group, we identified a group of 50 prognostic reporter genes that were highly correlated with the outcome (see Materials and Methods and Table S3 in Supplementary Information).' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/65/10/4059/517951); Materials and Methods, Kaplan-Meier plot: 'Only the patients belonging to the original 295 cohort samples were used for the Kaplan-Meier plot.' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/65/10/4059/517951)

development_data: 11-gene BMI1-pathway 'death-from-cancer' signature: genes concordant between metastatic TRAMP mouse prostate tumors and Bmi-1+/+ vs Bmi-1-/- neurospheres, reduced by correlation; the 11-gene MTTS/PNS variant was chosen among 3 candidate small signatures using metastasis-vs-primary discrimination and recurrence in human prostate cancer outcome set 1 (21 patients). For breast, the stratification cut-off (Pearson correlation threshold) was selected in the van 't Veer 78-patient training set by minimum log-rank P.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Prostate outcome sets 1 and 2; van 't Veer 2002 breast cancer 97 patients (78 training + 19 test, distant metastasis within 5 years); lung adenocarcinoma 125 (+ stage 1A 35); ovarian 37; bladder 31; also lymphoma (DLBCL, MCL), mesothelioma, medulloblastoma, glioma, AML in Table 2.
evidence: Results: 'Then small signatures (1 11-gene signature for the PNS set, 1 11-gene signature for the CNS set, and one 14-gene signature for the common PNS/CNS set) were tested for the power to discriminate the metastatic phenotype ... and therapy-outcome classification performance (using human prostate cancer therapy outcome set 1). Based on diagnostic and prognostic classification performance, a single best-performing 11-gene MTTS/PNS signature was selected for further validation analysis' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1136989/); Methods: 'We divided the patients within individual cohorts into a training set, which was used to select the cutoff threshold and to test the model, and a test set, which was used to evaluate the reproducibility of the classification performance. (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1136989/); Methods: 'The cohort of 97 breast cancer patients (shown together in Figure 7 C) was divided into a training set (78 patients; 34 poor prognosis and 44 good prognosis) (Figure 7 A) and a test set (19 patients; 12 poor prognosis and 7 good prognosis) (Figure 7 B) as described in the original publication ( 33 ).' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1136989/); Figure 7 legend: 'For each type of cancer, the patient’s stratification cutoff value was defined in the training set, validated in a test set, and confirmed in an entire cohort.' development_data: E2F1 target genes from rat REF52 fibroblasts infected with E2F1 adenovirus under serum deprivation, serum, or serum plus PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (Affymetrix RAE230A); PI3K-repressed (apoptotic) and non-repressed (proliferative) E2F1 targets (Tables 1 and 2) mapped to human U133A probes. No patient outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Breast: GSE1456 (Pawitan 2005 Stockholm), GSE4922 (Ivshina 2006 Uppsala), GSE2034 (Wang 2005 EMC); ovarian: GSE3149 (Bild 2006). Tumors split by unsupervised hierarchical clustering into 'high/low apoptotic' groups and compared by Kaplan-Meier survival (Fig. 5) and recurrence (Supplementary Fig. 2).
evidence: Results: "A total of 772 E2F1 targets that displayed at least a 2-fold increase in expression based on MAS5 data were clustered." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2243238/); Results: "The expression values of these E2F genes were then extracted from four different human cancer microarray experiments - three breast cancer tissue datasets ( GSE1456 , GSE4922 , and GSE2034 ) and an ovarian cancer dataset ( GSE3149 ) ( Bild et al., 2006 ; Ivshina et al., 2006 ; Pawitan et al., 2005 ; Wang et al., 2005 )." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2243238/); Figure 5A legend: "The two groups of breast cancer patients were designated either 'Low Apoptotic' and 'High Apoptotic' based on relative expression levels of the PI3K-repressed E2F1 target genes and were plotted according to patient survival in the Kaplan-Meier survival curve to the right." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2243238/)

development_data: 4T1 syngeneic mouse metastasis models gave a 79-gene spontaneous metastasis gene signature (SpMGS); the final six-gene model (Abcf1, Coro1c, Dpp3, Preb, Ptdss1, Ube3a; the Venet list) was then selected by per-gene multivariate Cox analysis of patient outcome in three human breast datasets: NKI 295 (van de Vijver), GSE4922 (163 Uppsala patients, after excluding 86 also in GSE2990) and GSE2034 (Wang, 286).
validation_data_named_in_paper: Training/'original' sets: van de Vijver NKI 295 (MFS, OS), GSE4922 163 (OS), GSE2034 286 (RFS). 'Independent validation-sets': GSE1456 (Stockholm, RFS), GSE2990 (Sotiriou 2006, RFS), GSE7390 (176 after excluding 22 GSE2990 overlaps, OS). Six lung cancer datasets (GSE4573, GSE11117, Director's Challenge HLM/MICH/DFCI/MSK).
evidence: Materials and Methods, 'Selecting the six-gene model from the spontaneous metastasis gene signature (SpMGS)' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2866744/): "To further evaluate the prognostic value of each gene within the signatures, intercohort multivariate Cox proportional-hazards analysis of each signature gene was performed in three breast cancer datasets. Genes significantly correlated with patient outcomes (p<0.05) were determined for each datasets."; same section (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2866744/): "12 of these had HR>1, of which 6 genes were predictive in all three datasets. This served as the logic and derivation of the new 6-gene model. Survival analysis was performed on the 3 original public breast cancer datasets (van de Vijver, GSE4922 and GSE2034 ) utilizing the 6-gene model. Additionally, the 6-gene model was tested against three additional independent public breast cancer datasets ( GSE1456 , GSE2990 and GSE7390 [footnote 3] )."; Results (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2866744/): "To evaluate the prognostic value of the metastatic gene signatures, and to determine which of the 79 SpMGS genes were more predictive with metastasis-free survival, we utilized three publicly available datasets of human breast cancer expression data and correlating clinical outcomes. These included the van de Vijver, GSE4922 and GSE2034 gene sets."; Materials and Methods, 'Published datasets: GSE4922 dataset' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2866744/): "Eighty six patients which overlapped with the GSE2990 dataset were excluded, leaving 163 patients in this analysis."; 'GSE7390 dataset' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2866744/): "Their analysis involved 198 patients of which we excluded 22 because of overlap with the GSE2990 dataset."; Results, 'Evaluation of gene signature and a six-gene model' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2866744/): "Therefore, the six-gene model was tested against 3 additional independent publicly available breast cancer datasets ( Figure 3 , bottom panel). development_data: The 13 known genes of the 8q22 'poor-prognosis genomic gain' region found by the ACE algorithm (expression scores = t-statistics of poor- vs good-prognosis tumors, smoothed along the chromosome) in three breast cancer data sets: van 't Veer 2002 (NKI), van de Vijver 2002 (NKI 295) and Wang 2005 (EMC 286). The region was retained because it was detected in all three outcome-based analyses.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Same three data sets (in-sample KM of high vs low 8q22 neighborhood score, Fig. 1C, Table S2); qPCR copy number in 36 microdissected tumors; FISH on a CINJ tissue microarray (82 tumors, metastatic recurrence); MTDH IHC on 170 TMA samples (metastasis and survival).
evidence: Experimental Procedures: "The expression score (ES) for each gene is first calculated according to the correlation of its expression with the phenotypes in comparison." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2676231/); Figure 1B legend: "Poor-prognosis genomic gain at 8q22 was detected in all three datasets ( van 't Veer et al., 2002 ; van de Vijver et al., 2002 ; Wang et al., 2005 )." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2676231/); Results: "Out of the five prevalent genomic events, the 8q22 gain was consistently observed in all three datasets ( Figure 1B ). We calculated the NS of this region for each sample in the three datasets, and used it to classify tumor samples into two groups with high and low NS. As shown in Figure 1C and Table S2 , the probability of metastasis-free survival of patients with a high 8q22 NS was significantly lower than the control group in all three datasets." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2676231/); Figure 2A legend: "Expression of the genes at the 8q22 region in poor-prognosis vs. good-prognosis samples of the three datasets." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2676231/); Results: "There are 13 known genes and 7 hypothetical genes in the 8q22 poor-prognosis genomic gain region ( Figure 2A )." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2676231/)

development_data: MCF-7 breast cancer cells: RARalpha/RARgamma ChIP-chip plus expression profiling after RA agonist treatment (Table S3, 1,413 RA-regulated genes; Venet list 1,345 symbols). No patient data used to define the gene set.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (van de Vijver 2002; OS and RFS, Figure 6C-D); GSE4922 Uppsala 249 (Ivshina 2006; RFS, Figure S14A); GSE2034 Rotterdam 286 (Wang 2005; RFS, Figure S14B). Expression-only use of UNC 146 tumors (Hu 2006) for subtype clustering.
evidence: Results, 'ERalpha and RAR-dependent gene regulation in breast cancer' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374131/): "We first examined the correlation between RA signature scores and clinical outcomes for a cohort of expression profiles from 295 breast tumor patients ( van de Vijver et al., 2002 ). A total of 354 putative RAR direct targets were identified in this dataset."; Figure 6C-D legend (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374131/): "Kaplan-Meier curves of overall survival (C) and relapse-free survival (D) among the 295 patients ( van de Vijver et al., 2002 ) classified by RA signature values."; Results (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374131/): "These results were confirmed for two independent breast tumor cohorts ( Figure S14 )."; Supplemental Experimental Procedures, 'Analysis of RAR binding and RA expression profiling on breast tumor samples' (https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0092867409005042-mmc1.pdf): "An RA signature score for each tumor sample was defined as Spearman's rank correlation between the RA-dependent gene expression profile in MCF-7 cells ... and the gene expression profile in the given tumor sample for all putative RAR direct targets"; same section (https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0092867409005042-mmc1.pdf): "The patient sample data were grouped into three categories based on their RA signature scores: P (positive RA score), N (negative RA score), and U (uncorrelated). The optimal two cutting-points of RA signature scores were determined by X-tile analysis (Camp et al., 2004)."; Figure S14 legend (https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0092867409005042-mmc1.pdf): "Kaplan-Meier curves of relapse-free survival for two breast cancer cohorts which contain 249 (Ivshina et al., 2006) (A) and 286 (Wang et al., 2005) (B) patient samples ... with accession number GSE4922 (A) and GSE2034 (B)"; X-tile is described by its authors as an outcome-based cut-point optimization tool (Camp RL et al. Clin Cancer Res 2004;10:7252, title: 'X-tile: a new bio-informatics tool for biomarker assessment and outcome-based cut-point optimization').

development_data: Uppsala cohort 249 tumors (GSE4922; U133A+B): PAM and SWS classifiers trained on histologic grade 1 (n=68) vs grade 3 (n=55) tumors; the 18-probe PAM set was chosen as the minimum grade-misclassification error (6-probe SWS set similarly). Labels were histologic grade only; no outcome used for gene selection, size or classifier choice.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Uppsala (DFS; all patients, untreated, ER+ endocrine-only; G2a vs G2b among the 126 G2 tumors and vs G1/G3); Stockholm 58 G2 tumors (GSE1456 subset; DFS in systemically treated and ER+ endocrine-only); Sotiriou et al. 2003 NCI (tamoxifen-treated); van 't Veer et al. 2002 (node-negative untreated); van de Vijver et al. 2002 (node-positive chemotherapy); Singapore 40 G2 tumors classified (no outcome).
evidence: Methods, Other data sets / accession: 'Uppsala and Singapore data can be accessed via series accession number GSE4922, Stockholm data is accessible via series accession GSE1456.' [original uses a semicolon after GSE4922] (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade); Methods, The PAM 264-gene classifier: 'Initially, we ran the PAM algorithm with all 44,928 probe sets as input in the Uppsala G1 to G3 comparisons and acquired a minimal set of 18 probe sets, which gave the lowest misclassification (error) rate: 3 of 68 for G1 and 3 of 55 for G3 predictions.' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade); Results: 'For the G1-G3 comparisons, maximal prediction accuracies were obtained with 18 probe sets (representing 18 genes) by PAM and only six probe sets (representing five genes) by SWS (Table 1).' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade); Results: 'Overall, Uppsala patients with G2a tumors showed significantly less disease recurrence than those with G2b disease (P = 0.001, Fig. 1B).' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade); Results: 'the genetic grade classifier was also predictive of recurrence in the Stockholm (G2) patients who received systemic therapy (i.e., chemotherapy, endocrine therapy or both, P = 0.027, Supplementary File 1F)' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade); Methods, Other data sets: 'The van't Veer et al. (3) and van de Vijver et al. (4) microarray data and clinical annotations were downloaded from the Rosetta Inpharmatics publications archive.' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade); Figure 2 legend: 'G2 tumors from each study were hierarchically clustered. Primary tumor branches (separating low and high expressors) were used to approximate G2a and G2b tumors for survival analysis.' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade); Results: '(Due to space limitations and high concordance between the SWS and PAM classifiers, only data for the SWS classifier are presented henceforth.)' (https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/21/10292/526291/Genetic-Reclassification-of-Histologic-Grade)

development_data: Mammospheres vs parental cells of four ER-positive breast cancer cell lines; the 200 most differentially expressed genes form the 'mammosphere-derived' gene set (Venet list 179 symbols). No patient outcome used for gene selection (abstract).
validation_data_named_in_paper: Two independent ER-positive cohorts, overall survival: dataset 1 = 122 ER-positive, adjuvant-untreated patients from NKI-295 (also 69 ER-negative NKI-295 tumors); dataset 2 = reportedly a consecutive NKI-AVL series of 129 ER-positive tamoxifen-only patients (1985-1994). Cohort details from search-engine excerpts of the full text, not read directly.
evidence: Abstract (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19353633/): "The 200 most differentially expressed genes between mammospheres and parental cell lines were used to generate a 'mammosphere-derived' gene set. Hierarchical clustering of gene expression profiles of two independent cohorts of primary ER-positive cancers based on the 'mammosphere-derived' gene set revealed that the subgroup of breast cancers with profiles similar to those of mammospheres has a significantly longer overall survival."; Full text (https://doi.org/10.1002/path.2544) not reachable (Wiley 403, no open-access copy per OpenAlex). Web-search excerpts of the full text state the gene set was applied to "122 ER-positive tumours of patients who did not receive any adjuvant systemic treatment (dataset 1) and 69 ER-negative tumours from the NKI-295 dataset" and to "a consecutive series of 129 ER-positive tumours of breast cancer patients, who received adjuvant tamoxifen only (dataset 2)" from NKI-AVL diagnosed 1985-1994 (excerpts not verified against the article).

development_data: UCSF / California Pacific Medical Center cDNA-array cohort (162 tumors profiled); 55 tumors with long follow-up split into good outcome (>=7 years disease-free, n=34) vs poor outcome (recurrence within 7 years, n=21); PAM, SAM and a van 't Veer-style correlation method each selected outcome genes, and the 21-gene set is their overlap. Not one of our cohorts.
validation_data_named_in_paper: van 't Veer 2002 breast data (NKI patients; n not stated in text) and Sotiriou 2003 PNAS (99 John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford patients, cDNA arrays); good vs poor prognosis classification and Kaplan-Meier survival.
evidence: Coding note (parent): NKI coded D because the classifier applied to the van 't Veer patients was refit on that cohort's own good/poor outcome labels (leave-one-out centroids), which the rule counts as fitting a model; the gene set itself was fixed on UCSF. ; Abstract (Methods): 'A subset of 55 tumors with extensive follow-up was used to identify gene sets that predicted outcome. The predictive gene set was further tested in previously published data sets.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855059/; Results, Outcome prediction: 'To identify genes associated with outcome, tumor samples from patients with seven year disease free survival versus patients having recurrence within seven years were compared.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855059/; Results, Outcome prediction: 'Thus, a fourth gene set was constructed consisting of genes that overlapped from the three earlier gene sets, resulting in a set of 21 genes.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855059/; Results, Comparison to published predictive gene sets: 'We tested the performance of our 21 gene set in the tumor sets of van't Veer et al. and Sotiriou et al. using PAM classification. The gene set classified 65% of the specimens correctly in the van't Veer tumor set, and resulted in significant differences (P < 0.005, Hazard Ratio = 2.76) in survival between good and poor prognosis tumor groups in Kaplan Meier analysis (Figure 4A).' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855059/; Methods, Statistical analysis: 'Classification of tumors for all gene sets was performed using a leave one out cross validation analysis based on correlation of each tumor's gene expression with the means of the remaining "good" or "bad" outcome tumors.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855059/; Figure 4 legend: 'Kaplan-Meier survival curves based on the 21 gene set in independent data sets. A) van't Veer et al. data set; B) Sotiriou et al. data set.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855059/

development_data: Invasiveness gene signature (IGS, 186 genes): genes differentially expressed (>=2-fold) between CD44+CD24-/low tumorigenic breast cancer cells (6 samples, from patients/xenografts) and normal breast epithelium (3 samples), Affymetrix U133A/B (GEO GSE6883). No outcome data.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 early breast cancer (van de Vijver 2002): overall and metastasis-free survival, patients split by correlation with IGS (>0 vs <=0), also combined with NIH criteria and with the wound-response signature; medulloblastoma, lung and prostate cancer datasets.
evidence: Abstract (Methods): 'We compared the gene-expression profile of CD44+CD24-/low tumorigenic breast-cancer cells with that of normal breast epithelium. Differentially expressed genes were used to generate a 186-gene "invasiveness" gene signature (IGS), which was evaluated for its association with overall survival and metastasis-free survival in patients with breast cancer or other types of cancer.' https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17229949/; GEO GSE6883 overall design (deposited by the authors): 'A gene signature was derived by comparing the gene expressions of 6 tumorigenic samples with 3 normal breast samples' https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE6883; Nature Clinical Practice Oncology research highlight summarizing the paper (secondary): 'The association between the IGS and outcome was examined in 295 patients with early-stage breast cancer from the Netherlands Cancer Institute database. Patients were divided into two groups: those with gene-expression profiles positively related to the IGS (correlation coefficient >0) and those with gene-expression profiles negatively related to the IGS (correlation coefficient <=0).' https://www.nature.com/articles/ncponc0764

development_data: Laser-capture microdissected normal, ADH, DCIS and IDC from 36 Massachusetts General Hospital patients (1998-2001), 12,000-gene cDNA arrays; genes correlated with tumor grade (grade I vs III) and up-regulated in the DCIS-to-IDC transition (Table 1, 39 genes; Venet's 30 symbols, e.g. IDH2, RRM2, TOP2A, BIRC5). Labels were grade and stage; no outcome data.
validation_data_named_in_paper: None (no survival or recurrence analysis in the paper; QRT-PCR confirmation of expression only).
evidence: Materials and Methods: 'All breast specimens were obtained from the Massachusetts General Hospital between 1998 and 2001' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC156311/); Results, Gene Expression Profiles of Breast Tumor Grades: 'we performed discriminant analysis and extracted two sets of genes, each comprising the top 100 genes correlating with grade I and grade III samples, respectively, from the 1,940 gene set' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC156311/); Table 1 title: 'Genes with increased expression both in high tumor grade and the DCIS-IDC transition' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC156311/); Table 1 footnote: 'The 39 genes shown here are those also identified in the 100-gene grade III signature.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC156311/)

development_data: Normal-tissue expression compendium of Ge et al. 2005 (GEO GDS1096; 36 tissues from 27 organs, Affymetrix): the 1% of genes most positively correlated with PCNA (131 of 13,077 genes); index = median expression of these genes. No patient outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (van de Vijver 2002; overall survival, also relapse-free survival) and Loi et al. 2007 GSE6532 (overall survival n=380 with 96 events, relapse-free survival n=393 with 139 events); meta-PCNA used as the adjustment variable and its own outcome association shown in Text S1 section 2.36.
evidence: Source note: No PMID in the Venet bundle; meta-PCNA is defined in Venet D, Dumont JE, Detours V. PLoS Comput Biol 2011;7:e1002240 (PMID 22028643, PMC3197658). ; Results, 'Meta-PCNA integrates most of the outcome-related signal': 'Ge et al. [54] profiled with microarrays 36 tissues from normal, healthy, individuals encompassing 27 organs. We call meta-PCNA the signature composed of the 1% genes the most positively correlated with PCNA expression across these 36 tissues (Table S1).' (https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC3197658); Methods, 'Meta-PCNA index': 'We computed the Pearson correlation between PCNA and all the genes in the Ge et al. [54] dataset and selected the 1% most positively correlated, i.e., 131 genes out of 13,077, to form the meta-PCNA signature' (same URL); Results: 'For the sake of simplicity, and because this is the most commonly used setup in the field, we focused on the 295 patients of the Netherlands Cancer Institute (a.k.a. NKI) cohort [2] and the overall survival end-point.' (same URL); Results, 'Results are reproducible across cohorts and end-points': 'We reran the analyses using recurrence-free survival, and on another cohort [56] using both overall survival and relapse-free survival.' (same URL); Methods, 'Expression data': 'Loi et al. [56] data were downloaded from NCBI's Gene expression Omnibus (accession GSE6532).' (same URL); Text S1 section 2.1: 'Graphics in the top rows are for the NKI cohort, and Loi et al. cohort in the bottom row, overall survival is the end-point in both cases.' (https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002240.s003)

development_data: Uppsala cohort, 251 p53-sequenced primary tumors (Affymetrix U133A+B; the GSE3494 patients, same Uppsala patients as GSE4922). Genes ranked by a linear model of expression on p53 mutation status with ER and grade as covariates; DLDA classifier size (32 genes) chosen by leave-one-out cross-validation accuracy for p53 status. No outcome data used for selection.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Uppsala 251 (disease-specific survival, in-sample; 67 ER+ tamoxifen-only subset); Ma et al. 2004 Cancer Cell 60 tamoxifen-treated (DFS, 22 genes); Sorlie et al. 2003 Norway 76 (DSS and DFS, 9 genes); van 't Veer et al. 2002 97 sporadic node-negative (5-year distant metastasis, 21 genes). p53 status (not outcome) also checked in Sorlie 69/44 breast and Chen et al. 59 liver tumors.
evidence: Abstract: 'we analyzed transcript profiles of 251 p53-sequenced primary breast tumors and identified a clinically embedded 32-gene expression signature that distinguishes p53-mutant and wild-type tumors' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1197273/); Methods, Patients and Specimens: 'Frozen tissue was collected from 315 consecutively presented primary breast cancers representing 65% of all those resected in Uppsala County, Sweden, from January 1, 1987 to December 31, 1989' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1197273/); Methods, Class Prediction: 'For gene selection, we fit a linear model to the expression data with expression level as the response and p53 status, estrogen-receptor (ER) status, and grade status as the predictor variables.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1197273/); Results: 'DLDA showed the highest sensitivity for detecting p53 mutants ... and was therefore selected for further analysis. By DLDA, the optimal classifier was comprised of 32 genes' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1197273/); Results: 'We next asked whether the p53 signature could predict disease-specific survival in the patients of the Uppsala cohort.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1197273/); Methods, Independent Datasets: 'The van't Veer et al. (21) data and survival annotation were accessed through the Rosetta Inpharmatics publications archive.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1197273/); Results: 'From our 32-gene signature, we were able to map 25 probes corresponding to 21 signature genes to all 97 tumors with outcome information. Unsupervised clustering revealed two primary and four secondary tumor clusters' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1197273/)

development_data: Breast cancer cell lines (Bild 2006 panel): 5 anchorage-dependent vs 8 anchorage-independent lines grown in standard culture; 200 genes most correlated with colony-forming phenotype, Bayesian binary probit model (Venet list 156 symbols). Validated in 42 ovarian cancer cell lines. No patient outcome used for gene selection.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Breast: GSE2603 (Minn 2005, MSKCC; lung metastasis and lung-metastasis-free survival) and GSE5327 (Minn 2007, ER-negative EMC; lung metastasis); lung GSE3593; melanoma GSE8401. None of these is one of our 13 cohorts.
evidence: Materials and Methods (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3008357/): "We generated gene expression signatures reflecting the ability of cells to grow in methyl-cellulose using gene expression data for 5 anchorage-dependent and 8 anchorage-independent breast cancer cell lines."; Results, 'A strategy to connect in vitro and in vivo cancer biology phenotypes' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3008357/): "To train the model, we selected cell lines with an extreme anchorage-dependence phenotype (less than 20 colonies) or an extreme anchorage-independence (more than 500 colonies). The expression pattern of the selected 200 genes showed a clear distinction between anchorage-dependent and independent cells"; Results, 'The anchorage-independent signature predicts the potential for metastasis' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3008357/): "We analyzed two breast cancer datasets in which DNA microarray data was available together with clinical outcome information."; Figure 4 legend (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3008357/): "Kaplan-Meier analysis based on anchorage-independent growth ability of GSE2603 ... and GSE5327 ... 'Low' (blue) and 'High' (red) are defined by being below and above 0.5 of predicted probabilities respectively, the optimal cut-off as determined by a receiver-operator curves (ROC) analysis"; Materials and Methods (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3008357/): "In this study we used four independent datasets of cancer with information for metastasis (breast ... GSE2603 and GSE5327 , melanoma ... GSE8401 and lung ... GSE3593 )".

development_data: Oncotype DX 21-gene recurrence score (16 cancer genes + 5 reference genes). Per the paper and the senior author's 2007 review, 250 candidate genes (from literature, genomic databases and published microarray prognosis studies) were tested by RT-PCR on FFPE tumors from three training cohorts (447 patients: tamoxifen-only arm of NSABP B-20, Rush Presbyterian, Providence St. Joseph); genes, regression coefficients and risk cut-offs were fit on those cohorts' recurrence outcomes. None of these cohorts is among our 13.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NSABP B-14 tamoxifen-treated, node-negative, ER-positive patients (668 evaluable of 675 blocks); endpoint distant recurrence (also overall survival). Not one of our cohorts.
evidence: Abstract (Methods): 'We tested whether the results of a reverse-transcriptase-polymerase-chain-reaction (RT-PCR) assay of 21 prospectively selected genes in paraffin-embedded tumor tissue would correlate with the likelihood of distant recurrence in patients with node-negative, tamoxifen-treated breast cancer who were enrolled in the National Surgical Adjuvant Breast and Bowel Project clinical trial B-14.' https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15591335/; Abstract (Methods): 'The levels of expression of 16 cancer-related genes and 5 reference genes were used in a prospectively defined algorithm to calculate a recurrence score and to determine a risk group (low, intermediate, or high) for each patient.' https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15591335/; Paik S, Oncologist 2007 (PMID 17602054), review by the first author describing development: 'Many genes identified as prognostic genes from microarray gene-expression profiling studies were included in this set of 250 genes. Three cohorts, including the tamoxifen-treated arm of NSABP trial B-20, were examined for expression of 250 genes. Correlating clinical outcome with expression levels yielded many prognostic genes from these three studies and the 16 top performing genes were identified for final model building and validation' https://academic.oup.com/oncolo/article/12/6/631/6410393; same review: 'Final validation of the RS was achieved by examination of its performance in a completely independent cohort from NSABP trial B-14, which was not used in the model building process.' https://academic.oup.com/oncolo/article/12/6/631/6410393

development_data: Stockholm cohort 159 patients (Karolinska 1994-1996; GSE1456; U133A+B): genes ranked by t-test between good and poor prognosis (distant metastasis or death within 5 years), DLDA, number of genes k=64 chosen by leave-one-out cross-validated error; risk clusters defined by hierarchical clustering of the 159 training patients.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Uppsala 76 node-positive adjuvant-treated and 135 node-negative untreated patients (5-year status, KM); van 't Veer et al. 2002 78 untreated node-negative patients (42 of 64 genes; +19 validation patients 'data not shown').
evidence: Source note: Venet PMID 16846532 is Calza et al. 2006 Breast Cancer Res (412 Stockholm+Uppsala patients), which validates the ~500-gene Norway/Stanford intrinsic set and defines no 46-gene list. Venet's 46 PAWITAN symbols (CDKN1C, HOXA5, IGF1, PDGFD, SLIT2, PTN, RUNX1T1/CBFA2T1, SETBP1, NOV, MFAP4, SCN7A, CLDN7, COL14A1, PRC1, DTL, ...) match the 64-gene list in Additional file 1 of Pawitan et al. 2005 Breast Cancer Res 7:R953 (PMID 16280042), which is the defining paper. ; Methods, Primary analysis and validation data sets: 'In order to maximize the statistical power, we initially used the whole Stockholm cohort (n = 159) as the training set for choosing an optimal gene set and identifying risk groups in the hierarchical cluster analysis.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1410752/); Methods, Primary analysis and validation data sets: 'poor prognosis was defined as distant relapse or death from any cause within 5 years of diagnosis' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1410752/); Results: 'The leave-one-out procedure (Additional file 1) suggested k = 64 genes as an optimal number of genes for separating the patients with good prognosis and poor prognosis, giving an overall error rate of 33%.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1410752/); Additional file 1: 'To choose the optimal number of genes, this procedure is repeated for k between 20 and 100.' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC1410752/supplementaryFiles (bcr1325-S1.doc, Additional file 1)); Methods, Primary analysis and validation data sets: 'To validate the results we used independent datasets from Uppsala, consisting of 76 node-positive adjuvant-treated patients and 135 node-negative untreated patients, and from the Dutch study of 78 untreated node-negative patients [16], referred to as the van't Veer data.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1410752/); Figure 5 legend: 'Supervised clustering of the van't Veer cohort (n = 78) using 42 genes of the 64-gene set.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1410752/); Calza 2006 (Venet PMID) Abstract: 'Using the intrinsic set of approximately 500 genes derived in the Norway/Stanford breast cancer data, we validated the existence of five molecular subtypes' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1779468/)

development_data: 128 genes distinguishing 12 metastatic from 64 primary adenocarcinomas (multiple organs, Global Cancer Map, Affymetrix Hu6800/Hu35KsubA; sample type, not outcome); reduced to 17 genes in a lung adenocarcinoma cohort (Bhattacharjee 2001, n=62) by signal-to-noise against two tumor clusters that differed in survival. No breast cohort was used for development.
validation_data_named_in_paper: van 't Veer 2002 breast (78 stage I node-negative training patients, time to distant metastasis, P=0.024); prostate (Singh 2002, n=21, PSA relapse); medulloblastoma (Pomeroy 2002, n=58-60); DLBCL (Shipp 2002, n=58, not significant); lung (Bhattacharjee, the reduction cohort).
evidence: Supplementary Information, I. Datasets: 'c. Breast - 78 stage I sporadic, primary breast adenocarcinomas with > 5 years clinical followup after lumpectomy. Clinical endpoint: Time to metastasis 3. See Dataset C. This study was previously published in 2002 by Van't Veer et al.' https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fng1060/MediaObjects/41588_2003_BFng1060z_MOESM1_ESM.pdf; Supplementary Information, III (Identifying the reduced 17-gene metastasis expression signature): 'We noted that 21 Affymetrix probe sets (corresponding to 17 unique genes) were significantly correlated with the primary lung tumor cluster distinction with a Sx > 0.4.' https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fng1060/MediaObjects/41588_2003_BFng1060z_MOESM1_ESM.pdf; Supplementary Information, IV (Applying the 17-gene metastasis signature to other solid tumor types): 'We mapped the 17-gene lung metastasis signature to the Rosetta platform using UniGene build #147, which resulted in 16 successfully mapped genes (Web Spreadsheet O). We then performed cluster / Kaplan-Meier survival analysis as described above using these genes (median polishing and average linkage clustering). Again, tumors bearing the metastasis signature at diagnosis were more likely to develop distant metastases than those lacking this signature (P = 0.024, Figure 3a and Web Spreadsheet P).' https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fng1060/MediaObjects/41588_2003_BFng1060z_MOESM1_ESM.pdf; Abstract: 'We confirmed this finding by applying the expression signature to data on 279 primary solid tumors of diverse types.' https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12469122/

development_data: Inducible human epidermal neoplasia model (ER:Ras-IkBalpha and Raf:ER-IkBalpha regenerated human skin grafted on mice); 737-gene core tumor progression signature (CTPS) = genes shared by the Ras and Raf epithelial signatures (Venet list 714 symbols). No patient data used for gene selection.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (van de Vijver 2002; survival and metastasis-free survival, Figure 3H, S2B); Sorlie 2001 Norway/Stanford breast data (survival and relapse-free survival, Figure S2C-E). Other epithelial tumor sets used for tumor vs normal separation only.
evidence: Results, 'Genes co-regulated by Ras and Raf during epidermal tumorigenesis define a clinically relevant core tumor progression signature (CTPS)' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3050547/): "A set of 737-genes, we term the C ore T umor P rogression S ignature (CTPS), was shared between the Ras and Raf signatures ( Figure 3F )."; same section (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3050547/): "To investigate the clinical relevance of the CTPS, we examined gene expression of the signature in a publicly available data set of 295 stage I and II breast cancers ( van de Vijver et al., 2002 ). Hierarchical clustering of the tumors based upon agreement with the CTPS segregated the tumors into two classes: 'concordant' and 'discordant' ( Figure S2A )."; Figure 3H legend (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3050547/): "Kaplan-Meier survival analysis (... Cox-Mantel log rank test) on 295 breast cancer samples hierarchically clustered and stratified into two classes based upon similarity to the 737-gene CTPS."; same section (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3050547/): "Analogous results were obtained for survival and relapse-free survival using an independent breast cancer data set ( Figures S2C, S2D, and S2E ) ( Sorlie et al., 2001 )."

development_data: Comparative meta-profiling of 36 cancer-vs-normal differential-expression signatures from 21 public microarray data sets spanning 12 tissue types (Oncomine compendium); genes significant (Q<0.10) in at least 12 signatures. Tissue-type labels only; no outcome.
validation_data_named_in_paper: No outcome validation. Leave-one-out cancer-vs-normal classification in 39 analyses and in 9 independent data sets (cancer vs normal).
evidence: Source note: Venet's 67-gene RHODES list matches the 'meta-signature of neoplastic transformation' (67 genes overexpressed in cancer vs normal tissue in at least 12 signatures, Fig. 2A), not the 69-gene undifferentiated-cancer meta-signature of the same paper. PMID is correct. ; Results: 'We began by metaprofiling 36 neoplastic transformation signatures from 21 data sets (overexpressed in cancer relative to respective normal tissue, Q < 0.10), which span 12 tissue types ... At the significance threshold of Q < 0.10, 183 genes were present in at least 10 of 36 signatures, 67 genes in at least 12 signatures' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC438973/); Figure 2 legend: 'Sixty-seven genes overexpressed in cancer relative to normal tissue counterpart in at least 12 of 39 “cancer vs. normal” signatures.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC438973/); Results: 'only 3 of 11 outcome analyses did, two of which compared poor outcome breast cancer with favorable outcome ( 14 , 15 )' [ref 14 = van 't Veer 2002 Nature] (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC438973/); Results: 'As described above, only 3 of 10 outcome-based analyses identified significant differentially expressed genes, and two were of the same cancer type, making it infeasible to attempt to define an outcome meta-signature.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC438973/)

development_data: 105 stage II, tamoxifen-treated Swedish (Lund, South Sweden Breast Cancer Group) tumors on SWEGENE cDNA arrays (GSE5325): 246 genes associated with PTEN IHC status (35 PTEN-negative vs 70 PTEN-positive) by 3-fold cross-validated Mann-Whitney ranking; SP/SA centroids defined by clustering in this cohort. No outcome used. Not one of our cohorts.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (van de Vijver 2002): DDFS and OS; Sotiriou 2003 PNAS (99 Oxford JRH tumors): RFS and BCS; prostate (79), lung (86) and bladder (80) datasets.
evidence: Results: 'Frozen samples for 35 PTEN-deficient (PTEN IHC-) and 70 PTEN-normal (PTEN IHC+) cases, matched on estrogen receptor (ER) status where possible ..., were selected for gene expression profiling. A 3-fold cross-validation strategy ... was applied to the microarray data to identify genes most significantly associated to PTEN IHC status' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855070/; Methods, Patient Material: 'Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor specimens were retrieved for 361 Swedish patients with stage II primary BC treated uniformly with 2 years of adjuvant tamoxifen' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855070/; Results, Clinical Implications: 'The Dutch 295 BC series (3) serves as a gold standard data set for independent validation (23). We mapped (24) our 246-gene PTEN signature genes to the Dutch data set and generated a nearest centroid classifier (NCC; ref. 2) trained on our data set.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855070/; Methods, Prediction of Signature Activation in Independent Data Sets: 'In brief, within each data set, matched genes were centralized, and for each classification, the SP and SA centroids were generated by using our data as defined in Fig. 1 B.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855070/; Results: 'We obtained similar results when classifying the data set of Sotiriou et al. (4) containing 99 British breast tumors.' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855070/

development_data: SAGE libraries of CD44+ and CD24+ cells purified from normal breast and breast tumors define candidate tags differentially expressed between cancer 'stem' (CD44+) and cancer CD24+ pools; the prognostic signatures 'A' (CD44+-specific) and 'B' (CD24+-specific) were then built from those candidates by (1) an expression-variability filter in Data Sets 1-3, (2) keeping probes with univariate Cox P<0.2 for distant metastasis-free survival in BOTH Data Set 1 (Wang 2005, GSE2034) and Data Set 2 (Sotiriou 2006, GSE2990, 125 node-negative untreated patients), and (3) hierarchical clustering in Data Set 1. Venet's 56-gene list is most likely signature A (CD44+ cancer cell genes such as SPP1, MMP14, PLOD2, HIF1A); signature B was built the same way.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Data Set 3, van de Vijver 2002 NKI 295 restricted to node-negative untreated patients (141 tumors): DMFS, RFS, OS; outcome also reported for Data Sets 1 (286) and 2 (125), and within ER+, ER-, low- and high-grade subgroups.
evidence: Supplemental Data, Microarray data processing: 'Three publicly available microarray data sets, each including expression data on frozen primary tumor samples obtained by surgery and follow-up clinical data about the patients involved, were downloaded: Data Set 1 (Wang et al., 2005) from http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2034, Data Set 2 (Sotiriou et al., 2006) from http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2990, and Data Set 3 (van de Vijver et al., 2002) from http://www.rii.com/publications/2002/nejm.html.' https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S1535610807000293-mmc1.pdf; Supplemental Data, Microarray data processing: 'Since Data Set 1 included only lymph node-negative tumors of patients who had not undergone chemotherapy or hormonal treatment, patients of this type were selected from the other two data sets for this study.' https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S1535610807000293-mmc1.pdf; Supplemental Data, Identification of signatures with prognostic relevance: 'Univariate Cox proportional hazards regression was carried out on the data for the probes selected from Data Sets 1 and 2 using R 2.2.0 ... to find probes that tend to correlate with distant metastasis-free survival time (time to distant metastasis or last follow-up). Probes with a Cox regression p-value < 0.2 (strongly or modestly associated with distant metastasis-free survival) in both data sets were analyzed further.' https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S1535610807000293-mmc1.pdf; same section: 'Only probes matching genes represented by remaining probes from both Data Sets 1 and 3 were kept for further analyses.' https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S1535610807000293-mmc1.pdf; same section: 'The represented genes upregulated in only the cancer-"stem" SAGE library pool were called signature "A," and the represented genes upregulated in only the cancer-CD24 SAGE library pool were called signature "B."' https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S1535610807000293-mmc1.pdf; Supplemental Data, Correlation of gene signatures with clinical outcomes: 'Signature "A" is consistently correlated with shorter times to distant metastasis, relapse, and death, while signature "B" is consistently correlated with longer times to distant metastasis, relapse, and death.' (Data Set 1: 286, Data Set 2: 125, Data Set 3: 141 patients) https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S1535610807000293-mmc1.pdf; Abstract: 'CD44+ cell-specific genes included many known stem-cell markers and correlated with decreased patient survival.' https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17349583/

development_data: Norway/Stanford cDNA data (115 tumors + 7 normal; locally advanced breast cancer series): ~500-534 'intrinsic' genes selected by low within-tumor variation across 45 paired pre/post-neoadjuvant samples; subtypes by hierarchical clustering; centroids from core samples. Venet's 15 symbols (KRT5, KRT17, CDH3, TRIM29, CX3CL1, CXCL1, FZD7, MFGE8, ANXA8, B3GNT5, CHI3L2, GABRP, SLPI, ...) correspond to the basal-subtype gene cluster (Fig. 1E, Norway/Stanford; a similar basal cluster is displayed for the van 't Veer data in Figs. 2F and 3B). No outcome used for gene selection.
validation_data_named_in_paper: van 't Veer et al. 2002 97 sporadic tumors (time to distant metastasis by subtype, subtypes assigned by correlation to Norway/Stanford centroids); Norway 72 locally advanced patients (overall survival, in-sample); West et al. 2001 49 tumors (no follow-up, expression only).
evidence: Materials and Methods: 'An intrinsic gene list was selected (534 genes represented by 552 clones ...), consisting of those genes whose expression varied the least in successive samples from the same patient's tumor but which showed the most variation among tumors of different patients.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC166244/); Figure 1 legend: '(E) Gene cluster associated with the basal subtype.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC166244/); Results: 'Hierarchical clustering was used, exactly as described above for the Norway/Stanford data, to display the expression patterns of 461 intrinsic genes in the 97 tumor samples that were obtained from patients diagnosed with sporadic cancer (Fig. 2).' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC166244/); Figure 2 legend: 'Branches are color-coded according to the subtype to which the corresponding tumor sample shows the highest correlation.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC166244/); Results: 'we performed a univariate Kaplan-Meier analysis with time to development of distant metastasis as a variable in the data set comprising the 97 sporadic tumors taken from van't Veer et al.' Patients were stratified according to the subtypes as shown in Fig. 2B.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC166244/); Materials and Methods: 'we used 77 of the 231 genes (77 genes overlapped with the Norway/Stanford data set) and performed a 10-fold cross validation leave-one-out analysis on the data presented in van't Veer et al.' [concerns the van 't Veer predictor, not the SORLIE genes] (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC166244/)

development_data: 99 patients (John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford, 1993-1994; node-negative and node-positive, mostly adjuvant-treated) on NCI 7,650-element cDNA arrays; univariate Cox regression of each probe element on relapse-free survival, 485 elements at P<0.05 (16 at P<0.001). None of our 13 cohorts.
validation_data_named_in_paper: No independent outcome validation of the 485-element list; survival associations shown in the same 99 patients. The van 't Veer 231-gene list (published genes only, no NKI data) was intersected with the arrays (93 probe elements) and tested in the 99 patients.
evidence: Source note: PMID is the correct paper (Sotiriou et al. 2003 PNAS). The label '93' is ambiguous: the paper's '93 probe elements' are the overlap with the van 't Veer 231 genes (56 unique genes), which cannot give Venet's 343 symbols. The only list in the paper of matching size is the 485 probe elements associated with relapse-free survival at P<0.05 (Table 9), which also fits Venet's content (PCNA, TOP2A, GSTM3, PRAME, RFC4, MCM6, MAD2L1, BUB1, CKS2; no ESR1, ERBB2 or TP53, as the paper states for the 485 list). ; Methods: 'Tumor samples from 103 patients with primary local breast carcinoma were accessed from the John Radcliffe Hospital from January 1993 to December 1994.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC193572/); Results, Identification of Gene Clusters Associated with Survival: 'A group of 485 different probe elements were identified that could separate RFS in the 99 patients with a P value <0.05, but only 16 probe elements were significant at the more stringent P < 0.001 level used to control for multiple comparisons (Table 9, which is published as supporting information on the PNAS web site).' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC193572/); Results: 'Of the genes reported to be associated with prognosis in breast cancer, only PCNA and topoisomerase II [alpha] were found to be elevated in the poor prognostic group (HER2-neu/basal-like). Interestingly, this gene list did not include the ER, Her-2/neu, or p53.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC193572/); Abstract: 'Of 231 genes previously reported by others [van't Veer, L. J., et al. (2002) Nature 415, 530-536] as being associated with survival, 93 probe elements overlapped with the set of 7,650 probe elements represented on the arrays used in this study.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC193572/); Results: 'We observed that 93 probe elements representing 56 unique genes overlapped' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC193572/)

development_data: Training set KJX64 (64 ER+ tumors, Oxford JRH and Uppsala, tamoxifen-treated; part of GSE2990): genes differentially expressed between histologic grade 1 (n=33) and grade 3 (n=31), 128 probe sets / 97 genes. Index scaling and cut-off (midpoint of grade 1 and grade 3 means, leave-one-out) use grade labels only; follow-up of KJX64 not used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: KJ125 (125 untreated Oxford+Uppsala, GSE2990; RFS), NCI (Sotiriou 2003), STNO (Sorlie 2003), NKI2 (van de Vijver 2002 NKI 295, treated and untreated subsets; RFS, and DMFS comparison with the 70-gene signature); 597 validation tumors in total.
evidence: Patients and Methods: 'We used five gene expression datasets obtained by microarray analysis of tumor specimens from a total of 661 patients with primary breast cancer: the training set KJX64, the validation set KJ125, the National Cancer Institute (NCI) dataset from Sotiriou et al. (14), the Stanford/Norway (STNO) dataset from Sorlie et al. (12), and the Nederlands Kanker Instituut (NKI) 2 dataset from van de Vijver et al. (15) (Table 1).' (https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/98/4/262/2521968); Patients and Methods: 'Microarray and clinical data for the 189 patients in the KJX64-KJ125 datasets are available at the Gene Expression Omnibus database (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo), with accession code GSE2990.' (https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/98/4/262/2521968); Patients and Methods: 'Our training set KJX64 was a part of a separate ongoing study on tamoxifen resistance that will be reported later [...] in this study, we used only information on ER status and histologic grade without considering the clinical outcome.' (https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/98/4/262/2521968); Table 1 footnote: 'Tamoxifen only, treatment is not relevant because the follow-up data from these datasets are not used.' [original has a semicolon after 'Tamoxifen only'] (https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/98/4/262/2521968); Patients and Methods: 'A gene expression grade index of zero corresponded to the midpoint between the average gene expression grade index values from histologic grade 1 tumors and histologic grade 3 tumors in a given population.' (https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/98/4/262/2521968); Results: 'To evaluate the gene expression grade index as a prognostic factor, we pooled data from our validation dataset KJ125 and the STNO, NCI, and NKI2 (which was split into treated [NKI2T] and untreated [NKI2U] subsets) datasets and examined the association between histologic grade and relapse-free survival' (https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/98/4/262/2521968); Results: 'We used the published cutoffs for the 70-gene signature, corresponding to a 10% rate of false-negative results, as previously described (15), and chose gene expression grade index cutoffs that produced the same number of patients.' (https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article/98/4/262/2521968)

development_data: HMLE human mammary epithelial cells induced to undergo EMT by Gsc, Snail, Twist, TGF-beta1 or E-cadherin knockdown; EMT core signature = 159 down- and 87 up-regulated genes changed at least 2-fold by all inducers (Venet list 242 symbols). No patient data used for gene selection.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI and UNC breast cancer datasets for survival (the EMT core signature 'failed to predict patient survival'); UNC/Hennessy subtype data and an MDACC neoadjuvant pCR dataset for expression/response associations (not survival).
evidence: Results (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2932589/): "We identified an EMT core signature consisting of 159 genes that were down-regulated and 87 genes that were up-regulated at least 2-fold by all of these EMT-inducing signals ( Table S1 )."; Results, 'Correlation of Expression of an EMT-Inducer with Patient Survival' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2932589/): "For this reason, we performed clinical prediction analyses on the breast tumors in the Netherlands Cancer Institute (NKI) and University of North Carolina (UNC) databases ( 49 , 51 ), using the EMT core signature. We found, however, that expression by a tumor of the EMT core signature failed to predict patient survival."; Discussion (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2932589/): "Surprisingly, we were unable to observe any correlation between expression of genes in the EMT core signature and a poorer survival outcome among breast cancer patients".

development_data: Six-gene miR-335 regulon: genes downregulated by miR-335 restoration in MDA-MB-231-LM2 cells (756 genes) intersected with genes upregulated at least twofold in both lung- and bone-metastatic MDA-MB-231 derivatives (116 genes). Cell lines only; no patient outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Combined MSKCC (Minn 2005, n=82) and EMC (Wang 2005, n=286) primary breast tumor cohorts, n=368, metastasis-free survival (Fig. 5d; each cohort separately in Supplementary Fig. 15). miR-335/miR-126 qRT-PCR in 20 MSKCC archived tumors.
evidence: Results: "The overlap between these two lists yielded a set of six genes for which expression is high in metastatic cells and suppressed by miR-335 ( Fig. 4a )." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2782491/); Methods: "The miR-335-regulated six-gene signature comprises the set of genes corresponding to the 756 miR-335 downregulated genes that (1) were also upregulated by more than twofold in both lung and bone metastatic MDA-MB-231 derivatives relative to the parental line (available gene expression data set 18 ) and (2) were expressed by multiple MDA-MB-231 cell lines." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2782491/); Methods: "The gene expression data sets from MDA-MB-231 cell derivatives as well as the primary breast tumour gene expression data sets from the Memorial Sloan Kettering (MSK) and Erasmus Medical Center (EMC) cohorts have been published previously 18 , 27 ." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2782491/); Figure 5d legend: "Kaplan-Meier curves for the combined Memorial Sloan Kettering and Erasmus Medical Center breast tumour cohorts (368 tumours) depicting metastasis-free survival of patients whose primary tumours expressed the miR-335 six-gene signature (positive) and those that did not (negative)." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2782491/)

development_data: Six direct miR-31 targets (FZD3, ITGA5, MPRIP, MMP16, RDX, RHOA) chosen from PicTar/TargetScan predictions and confirmed by 3' UTR luciferase reporter assays in MDA-MB-231 cells. No patient outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (van de Vijver 2002): metastasis-free and five-year overall survival by miR-31 target signature (Fig. 5A-B). miR-31 qRT-PCR in 56 Brigham and Women's Hospital patients (distant metastasis-free survival).
evidence: Results: "Reporter assays using miR-31-expressing 231 cells revealed that miR-31 repressed six of the UTRs: frizzled3 (Fzd3), integrin alpha5 (ITGA5), myosin phosphatase-Rho interacting protein (M-RIP), matrix metallopeptidase 16 (MMP16), radixin (RDX), and RhoA ( Figure 4A )." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2766609/); Results: "We determined if concomitant repression of Fzd3, ITGA5, M-RIP, MMP16, RDX, and RhoA correlated with disease progression in clinical breast cancers by examining expression profiling data from 295 primary breast tumors ( Table S4 ) ( van de Vijver et al., 2002 )." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2766609/); Experimental Procedures (miR-31 Target Signature): "Tumors were considered target signature-positive or -negative if the normalized expression of multiple of the six miR-31 targets herein identified resided in the top or bottom 15% of tumors in this cohort, respectively." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2766609/); Figure 5A legend: "Kaplan-Meier curves for 295 human primary breast tumors depicting metastasis-free survival, stratified based on expression of the six-gene miR-31 target signature." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2766609/)

development_data: NKI: 78 sporadic lymph-node-negative patients younger than 55 (34 with distant metastasis within 5 years, 44 metastasis-free for at least 5 years), Rosetta/Agilent arrays; genes ranked by correlation with 5-year metastasis status, 70 genes chosen by minimizing leave-one-out error, classifier threshold set on the same patients.
validation_data_named_in_paper: van 't Veer 2002: independent set of 19 young lymph-node-negative NKI patients (distant metastasis within 5 years). van de Vijver 2002 (the Venet PMID): 295 consecutive NKI patients, 151 node-negative and 144 node-positive (overall survival, distant metastasis-free probability), which includes 61 of the 78 training patients.
evidence: Source note: Venet bundle PMID 12490681 is van de Vijver et al. 2002 NEJM, which validated the already fixed 70-gene profile in 295 NKI patients. The 70 genes were selected in van 't Veer et al. 2002 Nature (PMID 11823860), which is the defining paper. Venet's 60-symbol list matches the 70-gene profile (for example MMP9, FLT1, CCNE2, ORC6L, SCUBE2, MELK, DIAPH3/DEPDC1). ; Abstract: 'Here we used DNA microarray analysis on primary breast tumours of 117 young patients, and applied supervised classification to identify a gene expression signature strongly predictive of a short interval to distant metastases ("poor prognosis" signature) in patients without tumour cells in local lymph nodes at diagnosis (lymph node negative).' (https://www.nature.com/articles/415530a); Supplementary Information, Method of supervised classification: 'We calculated the correlation between the prognostic category (metastasis vs. no-metastasis) and the logarithmic expression ratio across all 78 samples for each individual gene in the 5,000 significant genes.' (https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2F415530a/MediaObjects/41586_2002_BF415530a_MOESM7_ESM.doc); Supplementary Information, Method of supervised classification: 'The combined error rate reaches the minimum when we use 70 marker genes from the top of our candidate list. Therefore, we consider this set of 70 genes as the optimal set of marker genes that can be used to classify patients' (https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2F415530a/MediaObjects/41586_2002_BF415530a_MOESM7_ESM.doc); van de Vijver 2002 NEJM (Venet PMID) Abstract, Methods: 'Using microarray analysis to evaluate our previously established 70-gene prognosis profile, we classified a series of 295 consecutive patients with primary breast carcinomas as having a gene-expression signature associated with either a poor prognosis or a good prognosis.' (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12490681/); Note: Nature main text and NEJM full text are paywalled/403 from this host; the supplementary methods document is fully readable; the 61-patient overlap is taken from the established cohort overlap, not quoted from NEJM

development_data: Erasmus MC (Rotterdam) cohort, Affymetrix U133A, 286 lymph-node-negative patients without adjuvant systemic therapy (GEO GSE2034): 76-gene signature (60 genes for ER-positive, 16 for ER-negative) selected on distant-metastasis outcome in a 115-tumor training set. Not one of our cohorts.
validation_data_named_in_paper: Independent test set of 171 lymph-node-negative patients from the same Rotterdam series (GSE2034), distant metastasis within 5 years; subgroups (pre/postmenopausal, 10-20 mm tumors). Not one of our cohorts.
evidence: Abstract (Methods): 'We analysed, with Affymetrix Human U133a GeneChips, the expression of 22000 transcripts from total RNA of frozen tumour samples from 286 lymph-node-negative patients who had not received adjuvant systemic treatment.' https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15721472/; Abstract (Findings): 'In a training set of 115 tumours, we identified a 76-gene signature consisting of 60 genes for patients positive for oestrogen receptors (ER) and 16 genes for ER-negative patients. This signature showed 93% sensitivity and 48% specificity in a subsequent independent testing set of 171 lymph-node-negative patients.' https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15721472/

development_data: 271 genes differentially expressed (>2-fold, t-test P < 0.01, triplicate spotted arrays) between BT474 cells expressing constitutively active Alk5 T204D and BT474 control cells (GSE11293). The functional work used MCF10A/HER2 cells, but the expression signature itself was derived in BT474. No patient outcome used.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (van de Vijver 2002 / Chang 2005), RFS and OS by clustering and Cox (Fig. 9A-B); Harris et al. 22 HER2-positive patients treated with neoadjuvant trastuzumab and vinorelbine (response, clustering only).
evidence: Results: "an Alk5 T204D signature was determined by selecting genes that were differentially expressed between BT474/Alk5 T204D and BT474 control cells. The genes were filtered for expression changes greater than twofold in triplicate arrays with a t test P value of <0.01; 271 unique genes passed the criteria" (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2546920/); Results: "We next mapped the Alk5 T204D signature to a previously published 295-array data set by van de Vijver et al. ( 58 ) and Chang et al. ( 10 ). There were 90 genes of the 271-gene Alk5 T204D signature that demonstrated at least a 1.5-fold change from the median expression in at least two tumors." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2546920/); Results: "Cancers with a positive correlation with the Alk5 T204D signature had worse recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) rates than tumors with a negative correlation (RFS P = 0.05 and OS P = 0.01 by a log rank test) (Fig. 9B )." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2546920/); Figure 9C legend: "Hierarchical clustering of 22 breast tumors from patients who were treated with navelbine and trastuzumab ( 28 ) using 190 overlapping genes with the 271-gene Alk5 T204D signature." (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2546920/)

development_data: Three MSP-pathway genes (MSP/MST1, MT-SP1/ST14, MST1R/RON) chosen from mouse-model biology (MSP promoted metastasis in an MMTV-PyMT-derived transplant model). In NKI 295, MSP alone, each gene alone and every two-gene combination were tested against outcome and were not prognostic; coordinate above-mean expression of all three (MSP oligonucleotide 2 for presentation) was then reported.
validation_data_named_in_paper: NKI 295 (metastasis-free and overall survival, multivariate Cox, site-specific metastasis, combination with 70-gene signature); UNC/Utah 162 tumors (Perou/Bernard), relapse-free survival.
evidence: Results: 'we examined microarray gene expression data from 295 breast cancer patients from the Netherlands Cancer Institute studies ( 16 ). We found that MSP gene expression alone was not prognostic for outcome in human breast cancer (data not shown); however, because the biological effects of MSP depend on its proteolytic activation and the ability to bind to its receptor ( 2 ), expression of all three genes ( MSP , MT-SP1 , and MST1R ) would be required for activation of the MSP pathway.' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855278/); Results: 'overexpression of MSP , MT-SP1 , or MST1R alone, or any combination of two of these three genes, did not reveal any significant association with clinical outcome in this data set (data not shown).' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855278/); Results: 'Faced with uncertainties about which MSP oligonucleotide might provide the more decisive conclusion, we analyzed the results with all four possible permutations ... Every permutation revealed significant prognostic value when the three components of the MSP signaling pathway were expressed concomitantly ... we use the results with oligonucleotide 2 for illustrative purposes' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1855278/); Methods: 'Group A comprised tumors coordinately expressing MT-SP1 , MST1R , and MSP (according to oligonucleotide 2) at levels higher than the mean (43 tumors), and group B comprised the remaining samples (252 tumors).'
